questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The nature, the people, and the possibility for great biological studies.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was great meeting peple from all around the world, and I felt very motivated for my studies.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The MSU webside was not easy to find my way around, however we got emails with all the information and event invitations that we needed. I always had someone I could turn to for questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The Exchange coordinator at MSU had created many events for us, to connect.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Dorms around campus. There were many dorms.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: When applying for a dorm, you also had to apply for a meal card, for getting food in the food halls.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Most other students apply for meals every day of the week, so make sure to choose the 7-day meal plan.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were troubles with the website, and you had to have a health insurance before you could apply for courses. However even after I got my health insurance, I had trouble registering for classes.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to get a health insurance, and then you can start registering for classes. I think it was a rather difficult process, and it didn't work for me at all, so I had to ask the professors for help.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could ask the professors, and they send me through to the faculty leaders, and they could sign me up for my classes.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted. One of them were closed, but I emailed the professor asking if she could make an exception, which she was happy to do.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get you health insurance as fast as possible, and keep an eye out for the opening of class registration. Don't be afraid to ask for help!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took classes from both 2nd, 3rd and 4th year. And the 4th year class was definitely harder than the others.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different. There were a lot of hands-on education, and a lot of class discussions and assignments. I think it was a rather nice experience.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Beginners Yoga, Western Equitation, Equine Ethology, Ecological Responses to Climate Change, Habitat Inventory and Analysis.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely Equine Ethology and Ecological Responses to Climate Change. If you have a rather great knowledge of cow hold and grasses, Habitat Inventory and Analysis would also be good. The two other classes are active classes, and they have a lot of those, which is really nice.

questions.answer: I went to the doctors once, and had to pay 185$, however my insurance covered all of that.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The housing is inclusive the meal plan. And that was definately more expensive than I thought it would have been.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Literally all kinds.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hiking, go to Yellowstone. Find the groups for international students. Adventure hunters and 4N connection.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Yellowstone national park, Lava lake, horseback riding, road trip with your friends.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Focus on the other exchange students

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They are very polite

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Always ask, be kind to the professors (introduce yourself), go out

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting the other exchange students, and the studies

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Living with my roommate (I was very unlucky)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
